guide.title: Mendelssohn: String Quartet No. 2, Op. 13 – IV. Presto: A Listening Guide
guide.overview: This is a long, restless finale for two violins, viola and cello. It opens in E minor and spends most of its time in minor keys. It ends in A major, the home key. Listen for sudden swings between very soft and very loud. Listen for a long solo violin line before the calm close. The keys and chords here are estimated by computer, so small details may be imprecise.

listening_points.headline: A short introduction in E minor
listening_points.text: The movement opens in E minor with a short introduction. The second violin begins [m. 1]. Then the first violin takes the tune over accompaniment [m. 2-5]. It starts soft, then turns suddenly loud at [m. 6].

listening_points.headline: Whispering start of the main section
listening_points.text: The main section begins very softly at [m. 9]. The first violin probably leads. The music wanders through G minor, then C major, with a brief Bb major touch [m. 19].

listening_points.headline: A loud burst, then a bright turn
listening_points.text: The music gets louder in D minor [m. 25]. Then it turns to E major at [m. 27]. The first violin plays alone for a moment [m. 28]. A minor takes over from [m. 30].

listening_points.headline: The viola steps forward
listening_points.text: The viola probably has the lead for a few measures, though this is uncertain. The first violin gives way. The loudness drops from loud to soft at [m. 42].

listening_points.headline: The cello probably leads, with B major
listening_points.text: The mood goes soft and the cello is probably in front. At [m. 65] it plays solo. The key brightens to B major. The sound grows to mezzo-forte at [m. 68], then loud at [m. 71].

listening_points.headline: Fortissimo octaves, then a hush
listening_points.text: At [m. 86] the music is very loud. The parts play in unison or octaves [m. 87-89]. That means they play the same notes at the same or different heights. Then it suddenly drops to very soft in E minor [m. 90]. The first violin leads clearly here.

listening_points.headline: A loud solo that fades to soft
listening_points.text: The first violin plays solo at full force [m. 105-106]. A fade is marked at [m. 106], and the sound is soft at [m. 107].

listening_points.headline: E major glow and a growing sound
listening_points.text: The music settles into E major. It stays very soft at first [m. 120]. Then it grows louder at [m. 127] and reaches loud at [m. 128]. The first violin leads with confidence.

listening_points.headline: Dark and stormy in E-flat minor
listening_points.text: The key turns to E-flat minor, which often sounds dark. It is very loud. The lines move independently for a time [m. 134-137]. The cello plays solo at [m. 139].

listening_points.headline: The estimated loudest stretch
listening_points.text: The music builds toward very loud at [m. 158]. A computer estimate marks [m. 159] as the loudest and busiest point. The parts play in unison or octaves in [m. 159-162]. The key is E minor. Then it drops suddenly to soft at [m. 164].

listening_points.headline: A gentle viola solo in E major
listening_points.text: After the storm, the viola plays solo in a soft, bright E major.

listening_points.headline: Soft E minor, then louder
listening_points.text: After loud unison playing, the music drops suddenly to soft in E minor at [m. 239]. The first violin leads clearly with accompaniment. It turns suddenly loud (f) at [m. 243].

listening_points.headline: A calmer A major glow
listening_points.text: The music turns to a very soft A major. The first violin leads clearly [m. 333]. The texture is mostly chordal in [m. 334-340].

listening_points.headline: A long solo line fades away
listening_points.text: The first violin plays solo, very softly, for a long stretch from [m. 358]. It starts in A minor and passes through D minor [m. 363]. The new key signature at [m. 368] marks the start of the next section.

listening_points.headline: A slower close in A major
listening_points.text: The last section is marked Adagio come I. It begins in A major at mezzo-forte. The sound swells to loud at [m. 375]. It ends softly [m. 396]. The last measure [m. 397] is marked pp. The computer labels it tacet (no part playing), but chords are still detected there, so that label may be a reading error.

glossary.explanation: The home note and scale that a passage feels built around. Minor keys often sound darker. Major keys often sound brighter.
All the instruments play the same notes, at the same pitch or at higher and lower pitches.
The instruments move together in chords.
A measure in which no part plays.
